title: Session Delta Interchange Format & SDK Consistency — PRD (WIP)
content:
Overview:

This is a working PRD proposing a compact delta-first streaming interchange format (CDIF) and a corresponding SDK consistency model to support low-latency incremental output, deterministic resumability, and safer tool-calling in the Hosted API. The doc focuses on API-level framing (frames, checkpoints, tokens), developer ergonomics in client SDKs, and migration constraints for server-side runtime and router layers.

Why this now:
- Customers embedding interactive features report high perceived latency when the model waits for large tokens or full JSON outputs.
- Tool-heavy flows (search, DB writes, runner hosts) need deterministic replayable tool-call semantics to avoid duplication under reconnects and retries.
- Existing incrementally-streamed JSON and line-delimited workarounds are brittle across network jitter and mobile suspensions.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce median first-byte time for interactive flows by 30% vs current hosted streaming for lightweight responses (<= 64 tokens).
- Provide deterministic tool-call idempotency primitives that reduce duplicate tool side-effects under reconnects to <0.1% in spike tests.
- Offer a single SDK surface that supports: incremental text frames, typed delta patches for structured outputs, explicit tool-call lifecycle events, and checkpoint/resume semantics.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not mandate changes to the model output formats (LLM may still produce arbitrary text), it targets the transport/SDK contract and small server-side helpers (tokenizer-aware checkpoints).
- Not designing a full RPC system for heavy multi-step orchestrations — we target single-session, single-origin request flows.

High-level approach:
1) Define CDIF: sequence of framed "delta" messages where each frame is minimal (op + payload + optional logical offset + optional checkpoint). Frames are small and typed: TEXT_DELTA, JSON_PATCH, TOOL_EVENT, CHECKPOINT, HEARTBEAT.
2) Session checkpoints: server emits signed checkpoint tokens (opaque base64) that encode a compact cursor (model kv-checkpoint id, request id, output length, and a short integrity hash). Clients can resume by presenting the latest checkpoint.
3) Tool-call lifecycle: TOOL_EVENT frames include: tool-id, call-id, stage (call, started, result, error), idempotency_token (server-generated or client-supplied), and a replay-proof flag. Tools can be invoked in a sandboxed execution environment and must honor idempotency_token to be considered safe to replay.
4) SDK semantics: present both a streaming event emitter API and a consolidated typed-reconciliation API. The streaming API is an EventEmitter-like flow: on("delta"), on("checkpoint"), on("tool"), on("end"), with backpressure/ack hooks. The typed reconciliation API provides a final structured object built from JSON_PATCH frames and allows incremental reads.

CDIF Frame examples (conceptual):
- TEXT_DELTA: {op: "append", text: "hello"}
- JSON_PATCH: {op: "replace", path: "/summary", value: "short"}
- TOOL_EVENT: {tool: "search", call_id: "c-12", stage: "result", idempotency: "s-abcdef12", payload_ref: "ref://obj/345"}
- CHECKPOINT: {cursor: "eyJpZCI6...", seq: 42}

(Frames above are logical; wire format is newline-delimited length-prefixed CBOR/JSON depending on client capability; default: compact JSON with minimal keys.)

Key SDK ergonomics decisions:
- Default client binding will expose a small surface: startSession(opts) -> session.handle with: onDelta(cb), onPatch(cb), callTool(toolSpec) -> Promise, getLatestCheckpoint(), resume(checkpoint).
- Backpressure: session.ack(seq) can be called by the client to indicate it has processed up to a frame; server uses this to tune batching and live prefetch. Mobile SDKs will automatically auto-ack frames on main-thread idle to simplify integration.
- Partial structured output: JSON_PATCH frames follow RFC 6902 semantics; SDK must provide a "replayable object" that applies patches in order and allows read-through even if intermediate patches missing (returns undefined fields).
- Tool-call promises: every callTool returns a promise that resolves when a TOOL_EVENT with stage:result arrives or rejects on stage:error or session termination. If client supplies idempotency token, server prefers that token; otherwise server issues one.

Tool safety model and replay semantics:
- Idempotency token + deterministic call ordering: Router persistently stores call metadata for a short TTL (configurable, default 5 minutes). When resuming, presenting the checkpoint returns tool-call result events that already happened (server replays the TOOL_EVENT frames).
- Sandbox contract: tools invoked via hosted adapters must implement idempotent handlers for calls that are marked "replay-proof": the runtime will retry only when the tool's adapter declares safe-to-replay. For unsafe tools, the runtime will return an explicit error and avoid retrying.

Observability & Debugging surface:
- Per-session timeline: first-byte, last-byte, delta-frame counts, avg frame size, lost-frame/resend counts, checkpoint-generation latency, tool-call latencies, tool-replay events.
- New trace spans: "cdif:frame-emit", "cdif:checkpoint-issue", "tool:adapter-exec", correlated with request id and seq.
- SDK-level debug mode to capture raw frames to an S3-bucket or client-provided collector for offline replay testing.

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Backwards compatibility: support an opt-in header X-RI-CDIF-V1; without it we fall back to current streaming semantics.
- Gradual rollout: start with internal customers and a small partner cohort, instrument for frame-loss and duplicate-tool-call incidents.
- Runtime needs: small persistent metadata store for recent checkpoints and tool-call results (expected 100–500ms extra write on call path for durability). Consider using existing dedicated DB shards in Dedicated plans and a fast in-memory cache with write-behind for hosted.

Safety and rate limits:
- Each session may create tool-call attempts; to avoid amplification we introduce a per-session tool-call rate limit and an adaptive circuit-breaker on retries.
- Checkpoint tokens include a short-lived nonce; replay windows default to 10 minutes to prevent long-lived replay attacks.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 (prototype, 2 sprints): server emits TEXT_DELTA + simple CHECKPOINT frames; SDK live proof-of-concept in JS, immediate internal dogfooding.
Phase 1 (3 sprints): add JSON_PATCH, full checkpoint tokens, resume flow, and basic tool-event replay. Onboard a single partner for mobile.
Phase 2 (4 sprints): stable SDKs (JS, Python), telemetry dashboards, Public beta opt-in header.
Phase 3 (ongoing): broaden to self-serve customers, add GH integration for connector tooling, hardened sandboxing for tool adapters.

Success metrics (tracked per rollout):
- Latency: median first-delta time for interactive flows (target -30% from baseline).
- Reliability: percent of resumes that successfully reconstitute stream state (target > 99.5%).
- Safety: duplicate tool-call rate on reconnects (target < 0.1%).
- Adoption: percent of new streaming sessions using X-RI-CDIF-V1 after public beta (target 20% within 60 days of GA).

Open questions (blocking/needs decisions):
- Wire format: use compact JSON by default, or switch to CBOR for efficiency? Trade-offs: CBOR saves bytes and parsing time (mobile), JSON easier for debugging and proxies.
- Checkpoint token contents and crypto: server-signed vs HMAC — HMAC cheaper but requires shared key rotation rules.
- Tool-call persistence TTL defaults — 5m vs 30m for long-running mobile sessions.
- How aggressive should server-side replay be for tools that declare "best-effort" idempotency?

Appendix: developer examples and recommended integration patterns:
- Mobile: use session.resumeOnNetwork(reconnectHandler) that stores latest checkpoint in secure storage and resumes automatically when connectivity returns.
- Server-to-server: prefer presenting client-supplied idempotency tokens for long-running orchestrations.

Next steps (short term):
- Align with runtime/serving team on checkpoint storage constraints (meeting booked 2024-11-20).
- Prototype JS SDK surface and share with solutions engineering for mobile partner trials.
- Finalize a minimal wire format decision by end of sprint (2024-12-05).

Notes to self (working):
- Need a small compatibility shim for existing transcript ingestion in Console.
- Add example curl/websocket traces for PRD and include in public beta docs.
